next_question: Does per-type CV stability (≤0.5 at lambda=1) achieve at larger per-type n (500-1000/type) with KDE Scott or kNN k=5, or does kNN k=10 (EXPLORATORY CV pass max 0.470 at 250/type) survive confirmatory preregistration — and does the per-type vs pooled ordering reversal (KDE/kNN per-type>pooled vs binned pooled>per-type) persist across DGP families with different noise structures?
why_next: Two orthogonal paths are now available to advance the density-divergence research program: (1) sample-size scaling — KDE marginal CV fail (0.575, only 14.9% over 0.5) suggests 500-1000/type may achieve stability; (2) confirmatory kNN k=10 — EXPLORATORY CV pass (max 0.470, 8/8) at 250/type requires preregistration before claiming. The per-type vs pooled ordering reversal (KDE/kNN per-type > pooled vs binned pooled > per-type) is estimator-dependent and its generalizability across DGP families should be tested. Real Web DOM transitions remain the dominant unknown but require an estimator family that first achieves synthetic stability.

recommended_action: Design a Frontier experiment testing per-type CV stability at larger per-type n (500-1000/type) with KDE Scott and kNN k=5 on the same synthetic 2D [0,1]^2 DGP with 8 heterogeneous page types. KDE marginal CV fail (0.575, 14.9% over 0.5) suggests sample-size increase may achieve stability. The experiment should: (1) compute per-type and pooled-subsampled divergence at lambda=0 and lambda=1 with 500 and 1000 per type; (2) verify null control (per-type ≤ threshold at lambda=0); (3) check CV ≤0.5 at lambda=1 for all 8 types; (4) compare per-type vs pooled ordering at larger n. If CV passes at 500-1000/type, the per-type stability limitation is sample-size-specific. If CV still fails, the limitation is more fundamental to per-type heterogeneity. Do NOT repeat binned TV (tested three times). Do NOT move to real Web data until an estimator family achieves per-type CV stability synthetically.
